artists.biography:
Matthew Charles "Matt" Berry (born 2 May 1974) is an English actor, writer, comedian and musician. Berry is perhaps best known for his appearances in The IT Crowd, Garth Marenghi's Darkplace, The Mighty Boosh, and Snuff Box. He is renowned for his deep voice; he has voiced several advertisements, most notably for Volvic, The Natural Confectionery Company, Absolute Radio, and MoneySupermarket.

As a musician, Berry composed all the music for Snuff Box, as well as the music for AD/BC: A Rock Opera, which he co-wrote with Richard Ayoade. AD/BC was a half-hour parody of overblown musicals in general and Jesus Christ Superstar in particular, telling the story of the innkeeper who allowed Mary, Joseph, and the baby Jesus to sleep in his manger. AD/BC was broadcast in December 2004 and featured Fulcher and Mighty Boosh stars Julian Barratt and Noel Fielding. He also performed a song for an episode of Garth Marenghi's Darkplace entitled "One Track Lover", a spoof of cheesy romantic 80s songs.

perplexity.description:
Released in 2011 on Acid Jazz, Witchazel is the debut solo album by British actor and musician Matt Berry. The album blends elements of rock, pop, folk, and psychedelia, characterized by lush arrangements, baroque instrumentation, and Berry’s distinctive, rich vocal delivery. Drawing from British folk traditions and vintage pop sensibilities, Witchazel features a warm, nostalgic sound accented by acoustic guitars, mellotron, and subtle orchestral flourishes. Standout tracks like "Take My Hand"—which later became the theme for Berry’s BAFTA-winning TV series Toast of London—showcase the album’s melodic charm and lyrical wit.

Witchazel marked Berry’s arrival as a solo recording artist and established the musical direction he would continue to explore throughout his subsequent releases on Acid Jazz. It stands as a cornerstone of his discography, bridging his work in comedy and television with his passion for music. The album was well-received for its originality and craftsmanship, becoming Berry’s best-selling record and earning praise for its inventive fusion of genres. Its enduring popularity led to multiple vinyl reissues, but its initial 2011 release remains a defining moment in Berry’s musical career.
